sources.title: Smart Thermostats
sources.finding: ENERGY STAR describes heating and cooling as a major household energy use and smart thermostats that can automatically adjust temperature settings.

sources.title: Smart Home Tips for Saving Energy
sources.finding: ENERGY STAR describes scheduling, occupancy-based control, smart thermostats, and smart lighting as ways to reduce unnecessary energy use.

sources.title: Smart Lighting
sources.finding: ENERGY STAR describes remote control, schedules, occupancy sensing, and automatic shutoff as lighting controls.

findings.finding: Heating and cooling control is a high-priority household energy-saving area.
Smart thermostats can automatically reduce unnecessary heating and cooling operation.
Scheduling and occupancy-based control can reduce unnecessary device operation.
Smart lighting can use schedules, remote shutoff, and occupancy sensing.

requirements.requirement: The guide must be written for a Chicago apartment renter and distinguish actions the renter can take directly from changes that may require owner approval.
requirements.verificationMethod: Inspect audience, recommendations, and approval labels.

requirements.requirement: The guide must identify heating and cooling control as a high-priority household energy-saving area.
The guide must explain scheduling or automatic temperature adjustments when occupants are asleep or away as a way to reduce unnecessary heating and cooling operation.
The guide must include lighting controls such as schedules, remote shutoff, or occupancy sensing as applicable renter-controlled options.
The guide must not present unsupported savings percentages, utility-rate claims, or rebate claims.
requirements.verificationMethod: Search for unsupported numeric or financial claims.

requirements.requirement: The guide must include source references for externally governed factual claims.

requirementResolution.observedDefect: Some efficiency measures involve building systems a renter may not control.
requirementResolution.resolution: Recommendations identify owner-approval dependencies instead of assuming modification authority.

requirementResolution.observedDefect: Savings claims vary by building, climate, schedule, and equipment.
requirementResolution.resolution: The guide uses only quantities directly supported by controlling sources and otherwise describes relative opportunities without invented percentages.

tests.procedure: Verify renter audience and owner-approval distinctions.
Verify heating and cooling are presented as a high-priority opportunity consistent with SRC-EXT-001.
Verify scheduling or automatic temperature-control guidance matches the recorded sources.
Verify lighting-control examples are supported by SRC-EXT-002 or SRC-EXT-003.
Search for unsupported savings percentages, rates, or rebate claims and return VIOLATED if found.
Verify externally governed factual statements link to recorded authorities.

mutations.violationMode: Recommend changing building HVAC equipment without identifying owner approval.
Insert an unsourced percentage savings claim.
Remove source references from externally governed claims.
